headline: SECOND WEEKLY LOSS: Gold Clings to $4,200 as Warsh's First FOMC Looms — Iran Deal Caps Decline at 3%
snippet: Gold held above $4,150 support and recovered to $4,186–4,210 by Friday, June 12, but bullion is on track for a second consecutive weekly decline — down approximately 3% on the week, with silver off roughly 10% — as Iran deal optimism provided a floor but failed to erase damage from May CPI at 4.2% and blowout jobs data that pushed the 10-year Treasury to 4.58% and December rate-hike odds to 70%. Kevin Warsh's inaugural FOMC press conference on June 16–17 is the next binary event: markets price a 97% hold but the dot plot's framing — supply-shock inflation (gold-positive) or persistent demand-driven inflation (gold-negative) — will determine whether the structural bid reasserts into summer or whether $4,150 support gets tested again.

headline: IKKARI SEALED: Agnico Eagle Gets BC Supreme Court Final OK for Rupert Resources — C$3.00 CVR Sweetener Attached
snippet: The BC Supreme Court issued its final order on June 11, 2026, clearing the last legal hurdle for Agnico Eagle to complete its acquisition of Rupert Resources Ltd. — each Rupert share converts to 0.0401 Agnico Eagle common shares plus a contingent value right (CVR) paying up to C$3.00 cash over a 10-year term tied to production milestones at Rupert's flagship Ikkari Gold project in Finland. Securityholder approval was nearly unanimous (99.98% in favour on June 9), and Ikkari — one of Europe's highest-grade undeveloped gold deposits — adds a Tier 1 non-North-American asset to Agnico's portfolio at the closing of what will be one of the most strategically significant acquisitions in the global gold sector this year.

headline: 19 g/t AuEQ AT SURFACE, M&A FLAGGED: Troilus Expands West Rim Outside Resource — Analysts See Takeover Case Building
snippet: Troilus Mining Corp. (TSX: TLG) reported June 11 that drillhole WR-26-013 returned 6.93 g/t AuEQ over 18.5 metres — including 19.06 g/t AuEQ over 6.4 metres — and WR-26-014 returned 1.80 g/t AuEQ over 23.85 metres including 6.81 g/t over 5 metres, all from the near-surface West Rim Zone outside the current mineral resource but within 200 metres of the reserve pit in the 2024 Feasibility Study. Mining.com and the Northern Miner both flagged M&A implications: a near-pit, high-grade zone adjacent to permitted infrastructure in Tier 1 Quebec is the exact acquisition template mid-tier and senior gold producers are deploying capital to acquire, and Troilus already received US$1.3 billion in preliminary interest from state-backed export institutions in 2025.

headline: 9.7% Zn OVER 25m, KEY PERMIT IN HAND: BMC Minerals' Krakatoa Discovery Unlocks Yukon's $1B KZK Project
snippet: BMC Minerals (ASX: BMC) announced June 12 that the first drill hole at the Krakatoa Zone adjacent to the main ABM deposit at its Kudz Ze Kayah (KZK) project in Yukon — hole K26-560 — returned 25.1 metres grading 9.7% zinc, 180 g/t silver, 1 g/t gold, 3.4% lead, and 0.3% copper from 327.5 metres depth, confirming a new high-grade massive sulphide lens in the district. Simultaneously, BMC secured a key Yukon regulatory approval establishing the governance framework for acquiring remaining major licences, with the company targeting a final investment decision on the $1-billion-valued KZK project by late 2027 — a project that, in a Section 232 tariff environment that has structurally elevated North American base metals premiums, is now drilling into a more favourable fiscal landscape than when the feasibility studies were first modelled.

headline: 36.6m AT 4.0 g/t Au AND 1.0% ANTIMONY: Southern Cross Hits Critical-Metal Bonanza at Sunday Creek — 11 Rigs, 67 Holes Pending
snippet: Southern Cross Gold Ltd. (TSX: SVLB) released June 10 results from seven diamond drill holes at the Apollo and Apollo East prospects of the Sunday Creek Gold-Antimony Project in Victoria, Australia — headline hole SDDSC202 returned 36.6 metres grading 6.5 g/t AuEq (4.0 g/t Au, 1.0% Sb) from 700 metres depth, with peak sub-intervals reaching an extraordinary 493 g/t Au and 29.1% Sb. Antimony is on every Western critical minerals priority list following China's 2025 export restrictions, giving Sunday Creek's combined gold-antimony tenor a dual commodity value proposition that few active drill programs can match; with 11 rigs turning on a 200,000-metre campaign running to Q1 2027 and 67 holes pending assay, the discovery pipeline here remains very much open.

headline: THREE RIGS TURNING: Sirios Launches 25,000m Phase 1 at Cheechoo Gold — Quebec's 40-Million-Tonne Target Eyes 2027 PEA
snippet: Sirios Resources Inc. (TSXV: SOI) announced June 11 that the first phase of its fully funded 2026 exploration program is underway at the Cheechoo Gold Property in Eeyou Istchee James Bay, Quebec — two diamond drill rigs are already turning with a third scheduled before June 30, targeting a 25,000-metre Phase 1 followed by an additional 10,000 metres in early 2027. The campaign's primary objective is generating a new mineral resource estimate to support a Preliminary Economic Assessment targeted in H1 2027, working against a conceptual exploration target of 31 to 40 million tonnes at 1.27 to 1.45 g/t Au — a scale of potential that, at current gold prices above $4,200/oz, begins to have economic gravity without requiring high-grade bonanza intercepts.

headline: COPPER WALL UP: Trump's June 8 Section 232 Proclamation Hits Most Imports at 50% — Refined Copper Decision Due June 30
snippet: President Trump signed a proclamation on June 1, 2026 — effective June 8 — significantly expanding Section 232 copper tariffs: a 50% rate now applies to most copper articles and derivatives imported into the US, with a reduced 10% rate available for derivative products incorporating at least 85% US-smelted copper content, and expanded product coverage now includes additional industrial and HVAC equipment categories. The Commerce Secretary must deliver an assessment of the US refined copper market by June 30, at which point the President may impose additional duties on refined copper specifically — a deadline that, for junior copper explorers in Canada, Mexico, and the US building projects in 'allied' jurisdictions benefiting from partner-country treatment, creates a potentially material uplift to long-term copper price assumptions embedded in pre-feasibility and feasibility study economics.

headline: SIX NEW PORPHYRY TARGETS: Alkane's MMT Survey Remaps Boda-Kaiser District — Haddington Returns 1.74 g/t Au in NSW First Test
snippet: Alkane Resources Ltd. (ASX: ALK) released June 10 a regional exploration update from its Northern Molong Porphyry Project in New South Wales — a magnetotelluric (MMT) survey has defined six new high-priority porphyry copper-gold targets across the Boda-Kaiser district, and first-ever drilling at the Haddington prospect within the Comobella Intrusive Complex returned 3 metres at 1.74 g/t Au and 0.07% Cu. Diamond hole KAI226 also intersected a magmatic breccia root zone at 914 metres depth below the known Boda-Kaiser resource — a deep resistivity architecture characteristic of large-tonnage porphyry systems — supporting an interpretation of Northern Molong as a district-scale copper-gold system with multiple mineralising centres rather than a single-deposit asset.

headline: MOTLEY FOOL PICKS MP OVER USA RARE EARTH IN JUNE: Mountain Pass Scale, Apple/GM Contracts Give Decisive Edge
snippet: The Motley Fool published June 8 a head-to-head comparison of the two US government-backed rare earth producers: MP Materials (NYSE: MP), which operates Mountain Pass — the only large-scale US rare earth mine and separation facility — with locked-in offtake from Apple and General Motors plus established Commerce Department price-floor agreements; versus USA Rare Earth (NASDAQ: USAR), which holds the Round Top polymetallic project in Texas and received a $1.6 billion CHIPS Act investment commitment in January 2026. The Fool recommends MP Materials as the current better buy on first-mover advantage and revenue visibility — but notes that USA Rare Earth's heavier rare earth composition at Round Top (dysprosium, terbium, holmium) makes it the preferred exposure for investors specifically targeting HREE supply-chain resilience in the context of China's tightening export licence regime.

headline: LITHIUM BACK ABOVE $20,000: CME Hydroxide Contract Surges 86% YTD as Three-Year Battery Metal Bust Officially Ends
snippet: The CME lithium hydroxide futures contract has surged approximately 86% since January 1, 2026, crossing back above $20,000 per metric tonne for the first time since late 2023, as analysts across Reuters, Fastmarkets, and Mining.com declare the three-year lithium bust — which collapsed prices by up to 85% from 2022 peaks — effectively over. The structural catalyst is a forecast shift from multi-year global surplus toward supply deficit through 2026–2027, though disappointing Q1 2026 EV sales have tempered the recovery's pace; for junior lithium developers in the Lithium Triangle and Quebec's James Bay corridor — many of which shelved project development during the price collapse — prices crossing $20,000/t represent the minimum threshold at which new project financing begins to reopen.
